material_units.source_text: Going deeper — when may limits, sums and expectations be exchanged?
material_units.per_unit_reason: This literal heading poses a topic question about exchanging operations. It gives no condition or mathematical answer; those assertions appear separately in node893 and are reviewed there.

material_units.source_text: A limit and a sum cannot always be exchanged: for $a_{n,t}=1$ if $t=n$ (else $0$), $\lim_n\sum_ta_{n,t}=1$ but $\sum_t\lim_na_{n,t}=0$, although all terms are nonnegative. Two sums, or a sum and an expectation, may be exchanged when the terms are nonnegative (Tonelli), e.g. $\mathbb E\big[\sum_tX_t\big]=\sum_t\mathbb E[X_t]$ for $X_t\ge0$. A limit may be exchanged with a sum or an expectation under domination: $a_{n,t}\to a_t$ with $|a_{n,t}|\le b_t$, $\sum_tb_t\lt\infty$, gives $\sum_ta_{n,t}\to\sum_ta_t$, and $Y_n\to Y$ almost surely (Section 5) with $|Y_n|\le Z$, $\mathbb E[Z]\lt\infty$, gives $\mathbb E[Y_n]\to\mathbb E[Y]$ (dominated convergence; bounded convergence if $Z$ is constant). Nonnegative terms that increase with $n$ are another sufficient condition (monotone convergence).
